summary: Newton County tower near Racine: a 65-ft wooden tower was razed in 1964 and replaced by a 100-ft steel tower; the page lists the site as removed.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower erected in 1964 to replace a 65-foot wooden tower
facts.status_note: The Central US Lookouts page lists the tower as removed. The page gives no removal date.

events.note: Work on the Racine tower halted for lack of funds, per the Neosho Daily Democrat (July 23, 1947).
10-acre towersite acquired in fiscal 1948-49. The October 1948 report says plans called for a 65-foot observation tower; the page does not confirm that the wooden tower was finished.
Old 65-foot wooden tower razed at the site the day before the Neosho Daily News report of August 20, 1964.
100-foot steel tower erected at the Joplin Towersite, per the fiscal 1964-65 annual report. It replaced the wooden tower.

corrections.why: 19.8 m is 65 feet, the height of the old wooden tower razed in August 1964. The steel tower that replaced it was 100 feet (about 30.5 m), per the fiscal 1964-65 annual report and the August 20, 1964 newspaper report quoted on the page.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The page names the Missouri Conservation Commission for the 1947-1950 entries, but cites the fiscal 1964-65 annual report as the Missouri Department of Conservation's. The record keeps the earlier name; the page does not explain the change.

notes_for_editor: Single source: the Central US Lookouts page, which quotes 1947, 1948 and 1964 Neosho newspapers, Missouri annual reports and the official manual. The record's height_m 19.8 m (65 ft) belongs to the wooden tower razed in 1964; the correction proposes 30.5 m for the 100-ft steel tower that replaced it, which is the tower the page dates last. The completion date of the wooden tower is not confirmed. No removal date and no current-site information. NHLR and FFLOS have no Joplin entry. The 2022 MDC fire-tower article does not name this tower.
